title: Control what crosses (group filtering)
breadcrumb: Federation Hub: connecting multiple TAK Servers

headings.text: How this maps to Deploy App / Keycloak groups

blocks.html:
Connecting two servers with an edge is only half the story — you decide which data crosses it. Every edge has a group filtering mode, chosen when you draw it.

The four filtering modes

Mode Effect
Allow All Messages No filtering — everything on the edge crosses. Required for V1 connections and any V2 connection not running group mapping.
Allowed Groups Cross a message if it contains at least one of these groups.
Disallowed Groups Block any message containing one of these groups.
Allowed And Disallowed Groups Cross a message that contains an allowed group and no disallowed groups.

Prerequisite: the source node must be running group mapping to use anything other than Allow All Messages. If it isn't, your only option is Allow All.

How this maps to Deploy App / Keycloak groups

Inside each Deploy App deployment, Keycloak defines the groups and TAK Server uses them to decide who sees what (the In/Out/Both model — group, group_WRITE, group_READ — see Integrating to TAK Server → Keycloak). Those same group names are what the hub's edge filters match on.

So the hub lets you federate selectively:

  • Agree on a shared group name across the deployments that should share data — e.g. a COALITION group.
  • On the hub edge between them, use Allowed Groups = **COALITION**. Only data tagged with that group crosses; each deployment's internal groups stay local.
  • Use Disallowed Groups to carve out sensitive partitions that must never leave a deployment, even on an otherwise-open edge.

Because filtering is by group name, coordinate naming across the deployments you federate (a group only matches if both sides use the same name). The default anonymous group __ANON__ can also be referenced explicitly.

A worked intent

"Deployments A and B share a common operating picture for a joint operation, but keep their own internal traffic private."

  1. CA Group node for A, CA Group node for B (their CAs uploaded).
  2. Edge A → B and edge B → A (two-way).
  3. On both edges, Allowed Groups = **COALITION** (a group both deployments' Keycloaks define and assign to the relevant users).
  4. Publish the policy. Now only COALITION-tagged situational awareness crosses; each side's other groups never leave.
